characters.name: Steve Roberts
characters.arc: Protagonist — wants to fix the store to fix himself
characters.voice: defensive, jargon-laced when nervous, slowly becoming quieter

characters.name: Owen Roberts
characters.arc: Son — wants independence but craves Steve’s attention

characters.name: Marla Roberts
characters.arc: Wife — wants peace and creative expression

characters.name: Doug Miller
characters.arc: Veteran Clerk — wants stability and respect —  — — Active Arc: Doug takes charge of the demolition crew when Steve freezes, revealing he knows the building’s structural secrets better than Steve knows his own son.

characters.name: Piper Bellamy
characters.arc: Consultant — wants to prove her methodology works on any asset —  — — Active Arc: Piper arrives not to fire Steve, but to help him navigate the insurance claim, forcing her to confront the limitations of data in human crises.

characters.name: Mei-Lin Chen
characters.arc: Stock Manager — wants recognition for her organizational genius —  — — Active Arc: Mei-Lin reorganizes the chaotic salvage site into a functional workflow, saving the project from total disarray when Steve and Owen argue.

settings.name: The Flagship Store (Toledo, OH)
settings.description: A cavernous 1970s big-box structure smelling of wet drywall dust and ozone after the collapse, now a skeleton of exposed beams.

settings.name: Steve’s Kitchen
settings.description: Cluttered with unpaid bills and Marla’s rejected manuscript drafts, smelling of stale coffee and unresolved arguments.

settings.name: Owen’s Bedroom
settings.description: A fortress of LED strips and gaming peripherals, smelling of energy drinks and adolescent isolation.

settings.name: Torrid Home Regional Office
settings.description: A glass-walled minimalist space in Columbus, smelling of expensive leather and cold air conditioning.

plot_points.description: The roof collapses during a routine inventory check, trapping Steve and Doug in the aisles.
Owen films Steve’s breakdown in the parking lot; the video goes viral, stripping Steve of his dignity.
Steve buys work boots and quits his daily role, declaring a "sabbatical" to rebuild the store with Owen.
The first week fails catastrophically; Steve and Owen argue over blueprints, leading to a minor injury for Steve.
Doug reveals the original building plans were hand-drawn and hidden in the store’s old filing cabinet.
Owen discovers a talent for drywalling, finding a calm focus he hasn’t had since childhood.
A surprise electrical inspection threatens to shut down the partial rebuild; Steve must choose between corporate compliance and DIY improvisation.
(resolution, ch15) The store reopens smaller, with a new layout; Steve accepts that he cannot save everything, but he saved the core.

voice: Close third-person, past tense; a comedic-literary register that balances the absurdity of mid-American corporate culture with the tender, awkward reality of familial love.
